intervals.note: Bounds only: July 2002 is the start of the SNO phase of the project (the Picasso Lab runs in Montreal were earlier, undated); the founding date of the collaboration is not published. End: the November 2013 decision to merge with COUPP into PICO.
intervals.quote: In July 2002, a new phase of the project started. A batch of six 1-liter detectors with an active mass of approximately 40g was installed in a gallery of the SNO observatory in Sudbury

intervals.label: completed (merged with COUPP into PICO)
intervals.note: Month precision: the date of the news item announcing the decision. The same page says 'The new collaboration is called PICO'. PICASSO's final-results paper (2017) still describes 'the PICASSO experiment'. See the integrator note in the log.
intervals.quote: The PICASSO and COUPP collaborations decide to join forces !

name: PICASSO Collaboration
notes: No formation date or roster is recorded; the Atlas holds no memberships for it.

summary.plain: The international team behind the PICASSO droplet dark matter search at SNOLAB: physicists from Canadian, American, Czech and Indian institutions. In November 2013 it decided, with the COUPP collaboration, to join forces as PICO.
summary.technical: Collaboration of the Project In CAnada to Search for Supersymmetric Objects. Institutions on the official collaboration page (July 2012 listing): University of Alberta, Laurentian University, Université de Montréal, Queen's University, Indiana University South Bend, Czech Technical University in Prague, Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics (Kolkata) and SNOLAB. The collaboration merged with COUPP to form PICO (official news page, November 2013).
